3. The informant Md Nurul Haque (subsequently died), a son of the deceased Sobder Ali Mondol on 16-9-1997 lodged an FIR with Nowabgonj Police Station being Nowabgonj PS case No. 12 dated 16-9-2017 stating about the death of his father Sobder Ali Mondal impleading therein 35 (thirty five) FIR named and 60/70 unknown accused persons who were claimed to have been responsible for that incident and alleging in the FIR that the said accused persons had gathered at the place of occurrence on 15-9-1997 for committing offence under section 147/148/149/323/341/302/201/114 of the Penal Code read with section 3/4 of the Explosive Substances Act. He also alleged in said FIR that at noon about 1-30 on 15-9-1997 the informant and his brothers PW 1 Marfot Ali, PW 2 Ayesh Ali, PW 3 Amzad Ali and one of his cousin PW 6 Monsur, along with PW 4 Abdul Malek and his nephew PW 7 Monir were on their way to cultivate pulse seeds in their joint property situated at Mouza-Sekhalipur and while they reached south-west of their house, at the moment the accused Nos. (1) Md Fariduddin, (2) Amzad, (3) Mostaque, all sons of Haji Nur Mohammad, (4) Salam, son of Danesh, (5) Marfot Ali, son of late Ali Mohammad, (6) Naimul, son of Altab, (7) Salam, son of Emazuddin, (8) Malek, son of Mohammad Ali, (9) Altab, son of Ayenuddin, (10) Ayub Ali, (11) Moni, both sons of Altab Hossain (12) Hashim Uddin, son of late kcal) Ali, (13) Shafique, (14) Durul, both sons of Hashim Uddin, (15) Mokbul, son of Omor Ali, (16) Nurul, (17) Saidur, both sons of Mokbul, (18) Soibur, (19) Golap, (20) Jalal, all sons of Arshad Ali, (21) Komba, son of Zakatullah, (22) Noimuddin of villege-Harishpur, (23) Alauddin, son of Jan Mohammad, (24) Foyezuddin, son of late Siddique, (25) Nokul Chandra Mondol, son of late -Jogendranath Mondol,(26) Montu, son of Kalimuddin, (27) Baharul, son of Mujibur, (28) Saifur, son of Ayub Ali, (29) Meser, son of Toyab Ali, (30) Afsar, (31) Surut, both sons of late Saifuddin, (32) Kalu, son of Formez Ali, (33) Tota, son of Afan Ali, (34) Fekon, son of Gudu and (35) Alauddin, son of late Khalil, all of village-Sekhalipur, PS & District- Chapainowabgonj and other unknown 60/70 accused persons will be recognized by the witnesses, who in a preplanned and unlawful manner gathered there with common intention holding dangerous weapons in their hands like ea, kr1311, amt, 115MT, C411it etc. and had made obstruction on their way and made abuse words to the informant party saying “শালারা কাদের জমিতে কলাই বুনতে যাচ্ছিস আজকে শালাদের জন্মের কলাই খাওয়াইয়া দিব।”. Upon hearing such abuse words while the informant and his elder brother Marfot Ali revoked, at that time the accused Nos. (9) Altab son of Ainuddin, (12) Hashim Uddin, (15) Mokbul started dealting with lathi blow upon them and the other accused persons while tried to caught hold the informant's party but they by seeking others help went away to their houses. At that moment upon hearing their hue and cry the father of the informant, Sobder Ali Mondol coming out from his house while tried to obstruct the accused persons from their unlawful activities; suddenly, by an order of accused Md Fariduddin, the accused No. 2, Mohammad Amjad Ali by a "Hashua" in his hand dealt a cutting blow to the informant's father's belly which has caused Sobder Ali Mondol seriously injured and then while he felled on the ground the accused Surat, Fekon, Mostafa, Alauddin, Golap and Marfot throwing explosives towards the people gathered there and creating fear to the people present who being afraid by such act to save their lives fled away to their houses; however, taking that advantage the accused persons dragged away the dead body of the informant's father towards the Khalishpur village. 

 5. Upon such FIR an investigation was held by the police about to find out the prima-facie proof of the allegation and that is why the investigation at the first instance was held by one Sub-Inspector Md Zoad Mia of Nwabgonj Police Station and then by a police Inspector, Sheikh Ahsanul Kabir, the PW 9 who reportedly posted in DB of Chapainowabgonj and he after holding a perfunctory investigation into the case filed a charge-sheet on 6-5-1998 recommending therein 5 (five) accused persons, namely (1) Moni son of Altab Hossoin, (2) Shafiqul alias Shafiq, son of Hasumuddin, (3) Noimuddin, son of late Zillar Rahman, of Harishpur, (4) Fekon, son of Gudor and (5) Alauddin, son of late Khalil of village Sekhalipur, PS & District- Chapainowabgonj for holding trial against them; however, he recommended to discharge the other 30 (thirty) FIR named accused persons from the allegation brought against them in the case. But feeling aggrieved by the said charge-sheet dated 6-5-1998 the informant party filed a naraji and upon which vide memo dated 2-8-1999, a re-investigation of the case was held about to make investigation again into the allegation brought. Subsequently, to that effect, upon holding the re-investigation, another charge-sheet was submitted in the case by one Inspector Md, Moslem Uddin of CID, Chapainowabgonj who submitted the said charge-sheet on 7-6-2001 recommending therein for holding trial under sections 14/148/149/323/ 341/302/201/114 & 34 of the Penal Code against 35 (thirty five) accused persons as named therein including the names of the earlier recommended for discharging accused persons. 

 6. After submission of the said charge-sheet the case record was in due course transferred to the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Chapainwabgonj for holding trial and disposal of the case. Whereupon the learned trial judge registering the case as Sessions Case No. 40 of 2005 was while proceeded for holding trial but at that time upon a letter of the Ministry of Home dated 29-10-2003, the learned Public Prosecutor of Sessions Judge's Court, Chapainowabgonj has filed an application before the trial Court under section 494 of the CrPC for withdrawing allegation from the 30 (thirty) FIR and C/S named accused persons praying therein that they were implicated in the case upon a political biasness and therefore to escape them from political harassment the Government by the above noted letter has asked the learned PP to withdraw their names from the case and to that extent the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Chapainowabgonj i.e. the trial Court vide its order dated 12-7-2005 allowing the said application of the State has discharged the said 30 (thirty) FIR and C/S named accused persons from the case; however, by the same order the learned trial Judge directed to proceed the case against accused persons namely (1) Morn, (2) Noimuddin, (3) Fekon, (4) Alauddin and (5) Shafiqul holding that the case will be run against them in accordance with law and then fixed the next date for framing of charge of the case. Accordingly, the charge of the case was framed, in their absentia against the above named five accused persons under section 147/148/149/ 323/341/302/201/114/34 of the Penal Code on 8-2-2007. 

 7. In the meantime, the informant Md Nurul Haque had died and eventually, at the trial the prosecution has examined 9 (nine) PWs while the defence examined none and then upon relying the said evidence of the above 9 (nine) witnesses and also perusing the materials on record, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Chapainowabgonj vide the impugned judgment and order dated 31-10-2010 convicted the present two appellants only under section 201 of the Penal Code, even though charge and their examination under section 342 CrPC were held under several sections of the Penal Code and then sentenced them thereunder as aforesaid; however, acquitting the three others from the same charge as brought but finding no allegation proved, against them. 

 12. Mr Md SM Anamul Haque, the learned Advocate in supporting both the appeals, at the very outset, submitted that the charge as was framed in the case is a defective one; as because, no individual charge under section 201 of the Penal Code has been framed against the present appellants in passing conviction under the said section; however, in a general manner charge was framed under several sections in the case against all the five accused including the present two appellants and, as such, the defence could not be taken properly by the appellants in their pleadings to the extent of individual charge under section 201 of the Penal Code. He also submitted that the convict-appellants were also not properly examined under section 342 of the CrPC by showing about what evidence came forward to prove their individual involvement in committing such offence and, as such, the conviction passed later on against them under individual section 201 of the Penal Code is a defective one prejudicing the appellants; as because, the learned trial Judge in a general manner by filling up the prescribed form of section 342 of the CrPC and mentioning therein common implications under several sections against all the accused he has done the said examinations and therefore the charge under section 265D and examination under section 342 of the CrPC were not held properly in accordance with law and thus, those have been found very defective ones. He to that extent submitted that following the said defective charge and of examination under section 342, the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence cannot be sustained in the eye of law. Learned Advocate by placing his submissions in two appeals also contended that if so, the charge would be brought only under section 201 of the Penal Code against the present appellants, in that case, trial could not be held by the learned Additional Sessions Judge but to be held by a Magistrate. However, without doing so, the trial was held without jurisdiction. Learned Advocate also referring to the testimony of the PWs submitted that there are so money contradictions as they made in their evidence by each and every witnesses who by their testimony, long after more than 10 (ten) years of the alleged incident, have made some new embellishment and that is why the PW I Marfot Ali, the son of the deceased and the brother of the informant in his testimony, after more than 10 (ten) years of the incident has made out a new case before the trial Court which has not been supported by other prosecution witnesses. Learned Advocate then contended that no seized articles were placed and proved in the trial Court to identify those as claimed to have been seized from the place of occurrence in support of alleged murder. And therefore, to that extent the PWs 8 & 9 in their testimony said that “আলামত আসে নাই” 

 13. He also added to his contention that since against as many as 30 (thirty) principal accused persons the prosecution state has withdrawn the allegation even though each and every witnesses in their testimony and the Investigating Officer of CID in the re-investigation report categorically mentioned their involvement in committing murder of the deceased who were also later on at the trial found responsible by the trial Court, so far the murder of the deceased; but due to discharging them under section 494 of the CrPC they had not been bring into the book again. However, without bringing them into the book for their involvement in committing murder and leaving them behind, how the present appellants can be brought for convicting them under individual section 201 the Penal Code for allegedly causing disappearance of the evidence without proving the murder of the deceased, even discharging the said principal accused from the case. He to that extent also submitted that if, the principal accused are not taken into the book for adjudication who would be found responsible for committing the said murder. But without them and also without proving the capital offence of murder, how far the offence of disappearance of evidence or the deceased dead body can be taken into consideration for imposing punishment against the present appellants; even though other three accused who were on the same footing with the appellants have been acquitted by the trial Court from the same charge. Therefore, the learned Advocate in support of his above submissions referred to the case, reported in 2008 BLD 236, 44 DLR (AD) 60, 49 DLR .349, 1993 BLD (AD) 79 = 45 DLR (AD) 66, 1999 BLD (AD) 18 = 51 DLR (AD) 253, 13 MLR 303 = 60 DLR 371, 54 DLR (AD) 60, 2005 BLD 485 = 57 DLR 779 & PLD 1961 (WP) Lahore-167. 

 15. Learned Advocate finally submitted that since the latest Investigation Officer i.e. an Inspector of CID who upon a naraji after holding re-investigation of the case has subsequently submitted the charge-sheet recommending to hold the trial of the case against 35 (thirty five) accused persons, but at the trial he was not produced for giving his testimony in the case; however, the close relations who are most of them the sons and close relatives of the deceased and they are being interested witnesses by giving their testimony after long about 10 (ten) years of the incident had took revenge of their earlier enmity against the present appellants by implicating them as accused in the case; even though, as per the FIR version and as per the testimony of PWs-1 Marfot Ali it has been came into the light that when the occurrence took place the said witnesses had been fled away from the place of occurrence by the threatening of the principal accused persons. However, the learned trial judge without considering the said prevailing facts as well as the contradictions as appears in the testimony of the said witnesses but in a surmise manner has awarded the conviction and sentence against only the present two appellants under section 201 of the Penal Code while acquitting some others who were on the same footing and also discharging the principal accused under section 494 of the CrPC from charge of murder of the case. Thus, he argued that since the other accused persons who were on the similar footing had been being acquitted and discharged from the same charge brought against them and, as such, the present appellants cannot be convicted under the isolated section 201 of the penal Code without passing conviction for capital offence against the principal accused; even having therein no chain of evidence to implicate or entangle the present-appellants into the offence of disappearance of evidence, as above. Therefore, the learned Advocate urged that the said impugned judgment of conviction and sentence as being passed upon a wrong finding which is liable to be set-aside. 

 16. Mr Abul Kalam Azad, learned Advocate who appearing for the convict appellant, Alauddin in Criminal Appeal No. 8044 of 2010 supported the above such submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate Mr SM Anamul Haque and then he added to his submissions that there were two Alauddin in the case and that is why, the PW 8, Md Mansur Rahman in his testimony has clearly said- “আমি জান মোহাম্মদ এর পুত্র আলাউদ্দিনের কথা জবান বন্দিতে বলেছি।”The learned Advocate to that extent also submitted that since the present appellant's father's name is late Khalil, he will not be implicated and convicted in the case, as per the said version of PW 8. He also added that out of 24 charge-sheeted witnesses though only 9 were examined but among them the PWs-1, 2, 3, 6 & 7 are the family members and close relations of the informant while the others were involved with rivalry relation; because of, the informant party and the accused appellants were the supporter of two rival contesting local UP Chairman candidates and that is why the said facts of grouping between two rival Chairman Candidates have been clearly came into the light by the testimony of the prosecution witnesses. He further added that the PW 9 the first Investigating Officer of the case who in his charge-sheet had recommended to discharge the 30 principal accused persons from the case against whom the informant party filed naraji but only that I0 has come to adduce his evidence; however, the subsequent Investigating Officer, as worked in CID who upon naraji by holding re-investigation has sent up the all FIR named accused persons including the principal accused in the charge-sheet for holding trial against them upon finding their involvement in the alleged offence of murder was not produced by the prosecution to give his testimony in the Court. And then trial was though held upon recommendation of the said charge-sheet but the said 30 (thirty) principal accused persons were not bring into the book and the last IO of the case who worked in CID and finally submitted the charge-sheet upon holding re-investigation also was not produced as witness to prove the prosecution case. As such, the conviction awarded upon basing on and relying upon the testimony of some interested witnesses; even though, there were some contradictions in their testimony and particularly while no dead body or no seized articles as of the supporting evidence in proving murder or disappearance of dead body was not found placed in the case and that the principal accused against whom the allegation of murder was found proved but they were discharged from the said charge of murder under section 302 and therefore without taking those aspects into consideration but the conviction passed isolatedly under section 201 of the Penal Code against the present two appellants is appears to be a defective judgment and, as such, that judgment of conviction and sentence is liable to be set-aside. 

 17. In contrary, Mr Md Giasuddin Ahammed, learned Deputy Attorney-General who appearing with Mr Syed Bashir Hossain Chowdhury, learned Assistant Attorney-General for the state-respondent by referring to the evidence of the PWs as adduced in the case, submitted that since the prosecution witnesses have been able to prove the case against the present appellants under section 201 of the Penal Code and, as such, the said impugned judgment can be sustained without any interference; even if, a solitary eye-witness having been found reliable and trust worthy to award the said conviction and sentence. However, the learned DAG could not placed his submissions about to why the prosecution state has applied for withdrawing the allegation against the 30 (thirty) principal accused persons who were later On have been discharged from the case upon a prayer of the learned Public Prosecutor for the state; even at the trial their involvement in committing murder has been came into the light by the supporting evidence. 

 18. Even then, the learned DAG in support of his submissions referred before us the case reported in 5 BLC (AD) 86, 45 DLR (AD) 161 and 27 DLR (AD) 107 and to that extent he submitted that the conviction can be based only relying on a solitary eye witness and thus, there has been no illegality in passing the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence under section 201 of the Penal Code having finding some evidence thereto against the present appellants; even though the charge was framed under several sections but there has certainly been included the section 201 of the Penal Code. He also in support of his above contention referring to the case reported in 27 DLR (AD) 107 submitted that this Court may have to make its decision without sending the case back for re-trial about to re-examine the evidence again, if finding any defect but in that case, this High Court Division is very much competent to hold a decision on the matter upon re-examining the evidence again which are very much before the Court with the LCR. He therefore submitted that since the judgment and order of conviction and sentence was passed upon proper appreciation of the material evidence on record and also by making correct finding thereto and, as such, that judgment deserves no interference. 

 21. But the above such new facts has not been supported by any other witnesses among the other 8 (eight) PWs in their testimony as given in the Court. Rather, the PW 8, Md Monsur Rahman in his cross-examination has specified the two Alauddin's name saying “এই মামলায় দুইজন আলাউদ্দিন আছে। আমি জান মোহাম্মদের পুত্র আলাউদ্দিনের কথা জবান বন্দিতে বলেছি। আমি ঘটনার প্রথম থেকে শেষ পর্যন্ত ছিলাম ।”The above witness in his cross-examination also said that no seized articles (আলামত) was placed before them in the Court; even though he was one of the seizure list witness. However, though the 9 (nine) prosecution witnesses were adduced and produced their evidence in the trial Court in support of the prosecution case, but among them the PW Nos.1, 2, 3, 6 & 7 are being the family members and close relations of the informant, they are found very much interested witnesses and though they deposed in the Court but there have been so many contradictions about the name of the accused persons and they have also contradicted each other saying about who had dragged away the dead body of the deceased; even though as per FIR version and as per testimony of PW 1 all of them (witnesses) at that time had been fled away from the place of occurrence to their houses by the threatening of the principal accused persons. Even then, since the dead body was not found and the first 10, PW 9 was failed to hold a proper investigation about to tress out the dead body of the deceased and also how the murder of deceased Sabder Ali Mondal was held who however, recommending to discharge the 30 (thirty) principal accused persons against whom the specific allegation of murder was brought, by which the allegation of murder and of disappearance of the dead body was made very much questionable. Even though the said 30 (thirty) principal accused, after re-investigation and also by the testimony of the PWs had been found responsible for causing murder of the deceased. It also clearly reveals from the subsequent charge-sheet submitted after holding re-investigation, upon naraji, wherein the JO, an Inspector of CID namely Md Moselm Uddin submitting the said charge-sheet on 7-6-2001 has categorically mentioned therein that - জানা যায় যে, অত্র মামলার আসামী ফরিদউদ্দিন ১০ নং শাহজাহানপুর ইউ পির প্রান্তন চেয়ারম্যান । বর্তমানে উক্ত ১০ নং শাহজাহানপুর ইউ পি চেয়ারম্যান আঃ ওহাব । উক্ত প্রাক্তন চেয়ারম্যান ফরিদ নির্বাচনে প্রতিদ্বন্দিতা করিয়া পরাজিত হয়। ফলে দুটি দলের দলীয় লোকজনের মধ্যে দলাদলি শুরু হয় এবং উত্তেজনা বিরাজ করে। তাহাদের মধ্যে জমি সম্পত্তি লইয়া দুটি দলের মধ্যে মামলা মোকদ্দমা হয়। এই সমস্ত বিরোধের কারণে তার জের হিসাবে এই হত্যাকান্ড সংঘঠিত হইয়াছে।”Making such of his report the Investigating Officer finally implicating therein 35 (thirty five) accused persons' name against whom he has recommended to proceed the trial. But the prosecution without examining the said 10 rather, upon examining the above narrated questionable 10 as PW 9, and relying which the learned trial Judge has passed the impugned judgment upon making some incorrect finding and also by making out a wrong defence case, as well. 

 24. It also reveals from the record that the PW 9 Sheikh Ahsanul Kabir, appears to be the questionable 10 of the case who has recommended to discharge the principal accused persons' names from the case having finding no evidence against them to proof thereto; even though in the FIR, the informant has categorically with their specific participation mentioned their names therein and the said IO interestingly came forward to gave his testimony in the Court. However, after a naraji, the subsequent charge-sheet was though submitted by an Inspector of CID and following which the trial was held, who after holding re-investigation has bring up the above discharging 30 accused persons into the book again recommending to proceed the trial against them having finding their involvement in committing murder of the deceased Sabder Ali Mondal. But the said Investigating Officer of CID was not produced by the prosecution to depose in the Court; rather, the earlier IO an officer of DB, Sheikh Ahsanul Kabir who recommended to discharge the principal accused persons has came forward interestingly in the Court to depose his evidence in the trial Court, even then in his cross-examination he said that— 

 26. Where from he found that defence case, it could not be understand. It also reveals from the trial Court's order dated 8-2-2007 that the learned trial judge proceeded with the trial and framed charge against 5 (five) accused persons including the present two appellants in general manner under sections 147/148/109/323/341/302/201/114 and 34 of the Penal Code; even though he upon a prayer of the state vide order dated 12-7-2005 discharged the 30 (thirty) principal accused persons under section 494 of CrPC and then he finally convicted the present two appellants under section 201 of the Penal Code, however, acquitting the three others from the same charge; even their examination under section 342 of the CrPC was not held properly by the learned trial Judge but he held the same under the above noted all sections like framing of charge. Although, no charge was specifically or individually framed against them under the convicted section 201 of the Penal Code by specifying their involvement in committing that crime of disappearance of the dead body of deceased and/or showing disappearance of any such evidence. However, the learned trial judge vide his order dated 21-10-2010 has examined the present appellants and three others under section 342 of the CrPC by a general manner showing their implication under several sections of CrPC and then by filling up the prescribed form in similar manner like the charge framing order has examined them under section 342 of the CrPC stating that- “তদ্বারা আপনি দন্ডবিধির ১৪৭/১৪৮/১০৯/৩২৩/৩৪১/৩০২/২০১/১১৪ এবং ৩৪ ধারার শাস্তি যোগ্য অপরাধ করেছেন ।”But he finally without applying his judicial mind convicted the present 2 (two) appellants under section 201 of the Penal Code holding that— “ফলে আসামী নঈমুউদ্দিন ও পলাতক আসামী আলাউদ্দিনের বিরুদ্ধে দন্ডবিধির ২০১ ধারার অভিযোগ সন্দেহাতীত ভাবে প্রমাণিত হয়।”and then he convicted them under the said section, however, acquitting the other three from the same charge as brought against them; even though the evidence of grave offence under section 302 of the Penal Code has come against others who were discharged and acquitted from the case. The learned trial judge eventually frankly stated in his judgment, that— “কিন্তু দুর্ভাগ্যজনক হলেও সত্যি এই যে, উক্ত হুকুমদাতা ও হত্যাকান্ডে প্রত্যক্ষভাবে অংশগ্রহণকারী ফরিদউদ্দিন ও আমজাদ সহ মোট ত্রিশ জনের বিরুদ্ধে রাজনৈতিক ভাবে দায়েরকৃত হয়রানীমূলক মামলা হিসাবে ফৌজদারী কার্যবিধির ৪৯৪ ধারা মতে বিজ্ঞ পাবলিক প্রসিকিউটর এর আবেদন ক্রমে উক্ত আসামীদেরকে এই মামলা হতে ডিসচার্জ করা হয় । ফলে PW 1 সঠিকভাবে বলেছেন যে, যারা মাডার করেছে তারা নাই।” 

 28. But from the trend of deposition and cross-examination of the 9 (nine) PWs this Court finds there have been various contradictions about the fact and name of actual offender who were involved in taking part in murder of the deceased and of dragging away the dead body of the deceased but the learned trial judge disregarding the said materials on record, however, discharging and acquitting the other principal accused has convicted only the present appellants under a isolated section upon framing charge and examination of them under section 342 under common and several sections and basing and relying upon the un-corroborative evidence as given by even the family members and relatives of the informant who are the PW Nos. 1, 2, 3, 6 & 7 (who are very much interested witness) and they have been even though implicated the names of the separate sets of accused persons in the Court with some contradictions and making some new embellishment. The learned trial judge also disregarded the actual facts and of evidence of the case; whereas, the informant in the FIR stated and the PW 1 Marfat Ali, son of the deceased deposed in the Court, saying that upon a threat of principal accused they had been fled away to their houses from the place of occurrence when the incident of murder and dragging away of the dead body allegedly were took place. In that case, how they (the witness) had seen about the dragging away the dead body of the deceased, it could not be understand. 

 29. However, the learned trial judge upon misreading the said evidence and the materials on record and also upon non addressing the actual defence case but making out a new defence case in a wrongful manner which has/had no existence at all and then upon forming the issue of the case in a wrongful manner has passed the impugned judgment and order convicting the present appellants even though discharging and acquitting the others who were on the same footing. Thus, the said judgment has been vitiated by wrong findings and also non-framing of charge under the specific section of the Penal Code and wrongly examining the appellants under section 342 of the CrPC which has caused a miscarriage of justice. 

 31. Similarly, at the time of examination of the accused under section-342 if so, the particular incriminating evidence were not placed and put to the accused that also will have to cause a miscarriage of justice, seriously prejudicing the convicted accused. To that extent, in a similar situation a view has also been taken by our apex Court, in the case of The State vs Monu Miah and others, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 60, wherein their Lordships held as follows:— 

 "The examination of the accused under section 342 of the CrPC have been perfunctory which has seriously prejudiced the accused as incriminating evidence or circumstances sought to be proved against the accused was not put to the accused during examination under section 342 of the CrPC causing gross miscarriage of justice." 

 "In a case where bitter enmity is admitted between the parties it is required as a rule of prudence that there should be some such corroboration of the evidence of the interested witness as may inspire confidence in the mind of the Court." 

 "Thus, on a careful consideration of the eye-witnesses as discussed above, it is very difficult to rely upon their evidence in view of the glaring omissions and contradictions in their testimonies in Court. The learned Judge of the High Court Division have not considered the materials discrepancies, contradictions and omissions of the eye-witnesses in their judgment for which an error has crept in the judgment resulting in the conviction of the appellants."
